goal: Reduce JavaParserFacade fan-out by extracting method-resolution logic (methods that depend on MethodResolutionLogic and Collectors) into a new helper class so the facade no longer directly depends on MethodResolutionLogic or Collectors.

inputs: public MethodUsage toMethodUsage(MethodReferenceExpr methodReferenceExpr, List<ResolvedType> paramTypes)
ops.details: Create new class MethodResolutionFacade in the same package. Move the three methods that implement method-call and method-reference resolution into the new class, preserving their implementations. The new class will be constructed with the TypeSolver instance (TypeSolver typeSolver) and will use JavaParserFactory.getContext(...) and other classes as in the original implementations. Update JavaParserFacade to delegate calls to an instance field of MethodResolutionFacade (e.g. private final MethodResolutionFacade methodResolutionFacade = new MethodResolutionFacade(typeSolver);). Update imports in both files. This extraction removes the direct use of MethodResolutionLogic and Collectors from JavaParserFacade because those classes are only referenced by the moved methods; after extraction they remain referenced only by MethodResolutionFacade.

Add imports required by the new MethodResolutionFacade (e.g. MethodUsage, MethodResolutionLogic, Collectors, ResolvedType, etc.) and remove imports from JavaParserFacade that are no longer needed because of the moved methods.

inputs: java calls inside JavaParserFacade and external callers of JavaParserFacade.solve(MethodCallExpr, boolean)
outputs: callers updated to compile against unchanged public signature of JavaParserFacade
ops.details: Replace internal implementations with delegation so the public API of JavaParserFacade remains unchanged. Internal implementations should call methodResolutionFacade.solve(...). No external API change is produced; external code calling JavaParserFacade.solve(...) keeps working.
